claim: NBA's GAPC v4.0 (Revised NBA SAR 2025) defines 11 Program Outcomes for accredited Indian undergraduate engineering programmes, down from 12 under GAPC v3.
stance_target: current accreditation-mandated learning outcomes framework for Indian B.Tech programmes including ECE
scope_conditions: India, NBA-accredited UG engineering programmes, GAPC v4.0 aligned to Washington Accord 2021 review
quoted_support: NBA defines 11 Program Outcomes (POs) for undergraduate engineering programmes under the GAPC v4.0 framework (Revised NBA SAR 2025).

claim: The 12-to-11 PO reduction merged the old 'Society' PO and the old 'Environment and Sustainability' PO into a single new PO6, 'The Engineer and the World.'
stance_target: how NBA's outcome taxonomy changed between GAPC versions
scope_conditions: NBA GAPC v3 to v4.0 transition
quoted_support: This PO merges the old PO6 (Society) and old PO7 (Environment and Sustainability) into one.

claim: PO3, PO4, PO5, and PO10 explicitly require an engineering project/design experience to demonstrate: design of solutions, investigation using research methods, tool usage including modelling, and project management/economic decision-making.
stance_target: the major/capstone project is the primary curricular vehicle for demonstrating several NBA Program Outcomes
quoted_support: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and design systems, components, or processes to meet identified needs ... Conduct investigations of complex engineering problems using research-based knowledge and research methods ...

claim: POs sit as a middle layer between Program Educational Objectives (career outcomes 3-5 years post-graduation) and Course Outcomes (single-course achievement), with attainment rolling upward.
stance_target: the layered outcome-based education model Indian accreditation rubrics are built on
quoted_support: Program Educational Objectives (PEOs) describe career accomplishments 3-5 years after graduation, and Course Outcomes (COs) describe what a student achieves in a single course. POs are the bridge
